# quant-fidelity-suite — receipt-backed distribution-fidelity measurements

> Python/Bash measurement CLIs, capture datasets, and a schema-enforced registry
> for teacher-forced next-token KL divergence. The measured object is an exact
> reference/candidate pair on a pinned token panel and computational pipeline,
> not a universal model-quality score. MIT licensed.
>
> Start with WHAT-WE-MEASURE.md before citing a result. Use AGENTS.md when changing
> the repository. Historical plans, model-card prose, self-seals and green tests
> are not substitutes for the actual measurement and its disclosed limits.
>
> [QFS Explorer](https://huggingface.co/spaces/malaiwah/qfs-explorer) is the optional
> read-only web interface. Its cost calculator is not a runtime prediction or a
> spending cap; it neither rents compute nor accepts measurement credentials.

## Rules for reading a number

1. **Name the complete comparison.** Pin reference/candidate revisions, tokenizer,
   token histories, masks, scored positions, vocabulary policy, KL direction,
   estimator precision, capture lane, hardware, replay backend and quantization
   scope. The registry's comparability.key is a necessary partition, not a
   sufficient certificate. Check the secondary predicate and its reasons;
   unknown evidence does not authorize ranking. A different quantized scope can
   answer a product-comparison question, but not isolate codec superiority.

2. **Separate a panel census from inference.** More tokens are not automatically
   more independent observations. The historical Flash final25 panel has four
   source documents; clean17 has three. The newer corpus5x5 panel has 25 distinct
   document IDs, selected deterministically, and its receipt says calibration
   separation was not scanned. Other panels have other designs. Use actual
   document provenance, identify the sampling assumptions, and treat missing
   provenance as descriptive-only. Never use a single window or preview for a
   general rate ranking. A fitted-model coverage simulation does not establish
   deployment-population coverage.

3. **A control difference is not causal attribution.** Subtract only a control
   measured on the same panel, reference, scope of scored positions and lane.
   Report raw KL alongside any excess-over-control contrast. The difference is
   signed, can be negative, and is not itself KL or necessarily the part caused
   by quantization. The old 2.52x residual-ratio headline was withdrawn; do not
   resurrect it from a historical receipt, changelog or report.

4. **Say which computation was measured.** A checkpoint/reference-forward row
   reconstructs weights and measures that path. It does not automatically
   contain a native serving kernel's activation quantization or cache numerics.
   A hidden-form comparison applies the declared head to each sealed capture at
   the declared replay precision; it need not equal native bf16 logits. Retain
   weights_reconstructed / activation_quantization_not_captured disclosures.
   Pre-Hadamard decoder parity is not full native reconstruction parity.
   Weights-only KL is not a mathematical lower bound on served KL: additional
   perturbations can cancel as well as amplify differences.

5. **Repeatability is conditional.** Read run count, independent cold-capture
   evidence and tensor-content hashes. A zero self-comparison tests identity;
   it does not prove the capture is a correct model forward. Matching cold runs
   do not imply cross-device identity or add independent textual samples.
   Runtime and replay changes can move values; fingerprints cover only their
   recorded fields, not every possible confounder.

6. **Check the row's evidence class.** The registry includes modern pinned rows,
   historical float32_reduce_legacy measurements, unknown-precision third-party
   results, missing harnesses and incompletely available captures. Do not call
   all rows fp64, independently reproduced, or fully reproducible. A self-seal
   detects changes relative to a known digest; it does not authenticate who ran
   the computation or prove its correctness. Public reference data and candidate
   data are separate prerequisites for re-deriving a number.

7. **Do not substitute task quality for fidelity.** Lower reference-to-candidate
   KL on teacher-forced 2,048-token contexts does not establish higher task
   accuracy, safer output, better free-running generation, long-context behavior
   or a universal ranking of quantization formats. Unknown cross-stack or
   quantized-proxy bias has no guaranteed direction.

Safe claim shape: "On panel X, under capture/replay/hardware configuration Y,
this exact candidate had lower mean teacher-to-candidate KL than candidate Z."
Add uncertainty only with its actual unit, assumptions and evidence. Do not turn
that sentence into "the best quant" or a causal quality-loss ratio.

- [Measurement semantics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/WHAT-WE-MEASURE.md): estimand, heads, lanes, controls and inference limits.
- [Repository overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/README.md): navigation, capability matrix and entrypoints.
- [Contributor rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/AGENTS.md): editing, verification, money and publication boundaries.
- [Registry tables](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/registry/README.md): generated results and disclosures, not one universal leaderboard.
- [Published corrections](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/PUBLISHED-CORRECTIONS.md): additive corrections to prior claims; immutable receipts retain their historical bytes.

## Measure, inspect or contribute

Probe the actual command's --help before using a flag. Capability is route- and
artifact-specific: a decoder's existence, a published root, and paid admission
are three different facts. Panel fetch descriptors and dataset-route token
panels are also different mechanisms; there is no universal "one public panel"
rule. Inspect the current registry and exact pinned inputs.

- `bin/measure <hf-repo-or-url> --plan-only`: registry-first local planning, no rental. The target is positional; this command has neither --model nor --dry-run.
- `bin/measure-local`: local planning; --execute opts into execution and needs local inputs. A named GPU or memory budget is not a promise every model fits.
- `bin/measure-cloud --help`: paid controller contracts. Only run when explicitly authorized, first with --dry-run, explicit --max-cost and --max-runtime. Provider/parser support is not admission for every target or transport. Watchdog/reaper/provider guarantees have declared dependencies; do not promise an unconditional financial cap.
- `bin/fidelity-dataset`: capture, verify, compare and qualified publication. Capture once, compare retained datasets without re-running weights. Own-head comparisons include each capture's declared head; sharing a reference head can erase candidate head error.
- `bin/registry-view rows --model glm --lane streaming --registry local`: inspect the local snapshot without merging comparison groups.
- `bin/registry-submit <receipt.json>`: validate a submission locally; publishes nothing. Candidate comparison receipts and legacy submission receipts have distinct ingestion paths.
- [CLI reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/bin/README.md): route-specific commands and refusals.
- [First-time walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/THIRD-PARTY-QUICKSTART.md): prerequisites, safe dry-run and submission destination.
- [Contribution contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/registry/CONTRIBUTING.md): accepted receipt types, provenance and attribution.

## Machine-readable evidence

Prefer structured records to prose, but inspect disclosed unknowns and the
underlying receipts. The public mirror and this checkout can represent different
snapshots; state which one answered.

- [measurements.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/measurements.jsonl): values, estimator precision, uncertainty, determinism, evidence and disclosures.
- [artifacts.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/artifacts.jsonl): exact artifact and scope records.
- [panels.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/panels.jsonl): panel identity and declared availability.
- [references.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/references.jsonl): reference capture identity and availability.
- [pipelines.jsonl](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/data/pipelines.jsonl): declared runtime/hardware configuration.
- [index.json](https://huggingface.co/datasets/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-registry/raw/main/index.json): collection digests and group comparability predicates.
- [Schemas and invariants](https://github.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/tree/main/registry/schema): validator contracts.
- [Dataset format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/FIDELITY-DATASET-SPEC.md): capture seals, head policies and comparison gates.
- [Card format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/CARD-ANNOTATION-SPEC.md): machine-readable model-card provenance; a discoverable score is not automatically rankable.

## Deeper review

- [Joint protocol](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/PROTOCOL-ALIGNMENT.md): sampling, masking, intervals and explicitly bounded interop evidence.
- [Control experiment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/engines/BF16-FLOOR.md): same-lane controls and limits of subtraction.
- [Hardware sensitivity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE-DETERMINISM.md): measured devices, shapes and remaining extrapolation limits.
- [GGUF scope](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/GGUF-MEASUREMENT.md): whole-model versus routed-only quantization and effective bit rates.
- [Capture scaling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/docs/CAPTURE-SCALING-PLAN.md): measured scheduling experiments versus projected costs.
- [Campaign journal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/malaiwah/quant-fidelity-suite/main/JOURNAL.md): historical decisions, failed hypotheses and operational lessons; not current instructions.
